# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is the participant manual for the **MBAt Club Datathon 2026**
(Econometrics and Business Statistics), held Monday 21 – Tuesday 22 September at Learning and Teaching Building, Clayton campus.

It's a reference to work through **before** the event and to keep open
**during** the event — you're not expected to read it cover to cover in one
sitting, but every chapter should make sense as a standalone lookup when
you're stuck on something specific.

::: {.callout-warning title="Never push API keys or credentials to GitHub"}
Your team's repository is **public**. Your MongoDB connection string (and
any other password or API key) must never appear in a committed file — keep
it in a local `.Renviron` that stays out of the repo. See @sec-git-github
and @sec-mongodb-connect for the full setup.
:::

## How to use this manual

- @sec-code-of-conduct — the standards of behaviour we expect from everyone
  at the event, and how to report a concern.
- @sec-git-github — your team's submission is a public GitHub repository,
  so this is the one chapter everyone on the team should be comfortable
  with before Day 1.
- @sec-quarto — how to write and render the reproducible report and the
  presentation slides your submission requires — both are mandatory, not
  just for finalists.
- @sec-starter-template — the folder layout your team's repository starts
  from, and how to fill in and render it.
- @sec-sql-nosql and @sec-mongodb-connect — the competition dataset lives in
  a MongoDB Atlas cluster; these two chapters cover the concepts and the
  hands-on connection guide for pulling it into R.
- @sec-tidytext — further reading and techniques for text mining the
  (mostly free-text) dataset, beyond what's already worked through in the
  MongoDB chapter.
- @sec-viz-tables — turning your analysis into a figure or table a judge
  can actually read at a glance: choosing the right chart, designing for
  perception, and building a communicative table from a fitted model.

## Before you arrive

- Install R, RStudio (or Positron/VS Code with the R extension), Quarto, and
  GitHub Desktop.
- Create a GitHub account if you don't already have one, and share your
  username with organisers — they create and share your team's repository,
  so you just need to clone it (@sec-git-github).
- Skim @sec-git-github and @sec-quarto ahead of time — Day 1 morning is
  registration, opening remarks, and the dataset introduction, and the
  working session doesn't start until 10:30 AM, so setup issues are much
  cheaper to fix beforehand than mid-competition.

## Getting help on the day

A help desk is staffed for the full duration of both days. If you're stuck
on something in this manual for more than a few minutes, ask rather than
losing working time to it.
